title: Decentralized Command
coreMove: give local leaders intent, limits, and standards so they can decide without waiting for permission
sourcePressure: Leaders must train and trust junior leaders so decisions happen close to the facts instead of bottlenecking at the top.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: delegate tasks and hope people figure it out
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

counterintuition: leadership is harder than it looks
tryThisNow: ask yourself how to be a better leader

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

exampleSpecs.domain: orchard harvest as frost forms before dawn
exampleSpecs.audience: an orchard manager who cannot be in every block at once
exampleSpecs.stakes: waiting for central permission can lose fruit across the lower rows
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager gives block leads the frost threshold, fan-start limits, and quality standard the night before, then lets the north-block lead start fans without a call
exampleSpecs.firstImage: white frost beads on a low apple branch beside a sensor stake

exampleSpecs.domain: marathon medical coverage along a city route
exampleSpecs.audience: an EMS coordinator with aid stations spread over twenty-six miles
exampleSpecs.stakes: central approval delays care when runners collapse far from command
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coordinator gives station captains treatment limits, transport triggers, and radio escalation rules before the race, then backs the mile-eight captain’s call
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are close enough to see this: mile-eight banner snaps above a folding cot near the curb.

exampleSpecs.domain: SaaS outage where support leads see customer patterns first
exampleSpecs.audience: a customer operations director above regional support leads
exampleSpecs.stakes: customer harm grows if every concession waits for executive approval
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director gives support leads a credit limit, message intent, and escalation boundary, then lets the Brazil lead handle a key account live
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The first thing you register is physical: priority customer chat turns purple in the regional support queue.

exampleSpecs.domain: touring concert crew facing a weather delay at an outdoor venue
exampleSpecs.audience: a production director with rigging, sound, and security teams spread across the site
exampleSpecs.stakes: a storm cell can make waiting for one command channel unsafe
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director briefs team leads on go/no-go criteria, protected equipment priorities, and stop-work authority, then lets rigging call a pause from the roofline
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Hold there," someone says. Wind meter clicks against the truss while tarps flap below.

exampleSpecs.domain: field archaeology dig when a trench exposes unexpected human remains
exampleSpecs.audience: a site director supervising crews across several trenches
exampleSpecs.stakes: legal and ethical handling can fail if junior trench leads wait too long
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director had already trained trench leads on stop-work signs and reporting limits, so the junior lead covers the find, halts the trench, and calls the designated authority without asking first
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Later, the team will trace the lesson back to this: square trowel pauses above a pale curved fragment in the trench wall.

exampleSpecs.domain: concrete pour for a hospital foundation
exampleSpecs.audience: a site superintendent with inspectors at separate pour zones
exampleSpecs.stakes: a bad slump test in one zone can compromise a critical foundation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the superintendent gives inspectors reject authority and the project intent, then the east-zone inspector stops one truck before the superintendent arrives
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What changes once this is in front of everyone: wet concrete slumps over a cone beside the east-zone formwork?

skillTargets: set intent, limits, and standards before decentralizing authority
choose when to back a local leader’s bounded call

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one decision you still centralize, then write the intent, limit, and standard someone else would need to make it without you.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
